_comment: Lunda Grade 1 Teacher's Guide — per-book overrides.
Sibling of LUNDA GRADE 1 LB (same author, same 14 CHIBALU units, same
numbering). Anything decided for one of the two should hold for the other.
Every `find` string below is copied from the IMPORTED text (the engine's own
_last-docx.typ dump), not from the manuscript.md rendering, so the characters
are the ones the engine actually sees.
_note_authors: The manuscript names the same person two ways: its own title-page line reads
'C.K. KABALAKANYA' while the ANSONEKI page gives him in full as 'Charles
Kazembe Kabalakanya, Managing Director/CEO Wa Charle-Charle General Dealers
Company Limited'. House style is one form per person, the fullest one, so the
cover and title-page byline carry the full name rather than the initials the
author happened to type on his own cover page. The Learner's Book carries the
_note_localLabels: Cover, title page and spine words in Lunda, as the Lunda Grade 1 LB prints them (no English on a local-language cover).
_note_coverWords: Book type as the manuscript's own cover prints it, "MUKANDA WA NTAÑISHI" (also on the 6 Oct build and the author's returned FINAL BOOK), not the word list's "MUKANDA WAKULOMBOLA NTAÑISHI". Back cover "Published by", the house standard.
_note_boxActivities: The author typed every activity as a bold heading ('Zhakwila 1: Kubakula ni
kuzhika mukanda') with its instructions as plain paragraphs under it, rather
than in the shaded single-cell table other books use. Left alone the engine
renders them as ordinary headings, so an activity is indistinguishable from
the section headings around it, and the three casings the author used —
'Zhakwila 2: Kumwekesha Mwazatikilaña ni Mwatalisha Mazu' (p122) — print as
three different-looking elements for one thing.
boxActivities boxes all 151 of them and lets uniformBoxLabelCase settle the
label on one case throughout, which is how the sibling Kiikaonde Grade 1
Teacher's Guide renders (there via the kaonde THEME flag). It is set per-book
rather than on the lunda theme because that theme is shared with the Lunda
Grade 1 Learner's Book, which should not take a Teacher's Guide's boxing.
_note_asHead: AUTHOR SLIP CORRECTED, one activity. Every other activity in the book is a
bold heading of its own with its instruction in the paragraph below. In the
KUTIYILILA KUNSAÑU lesson of CHIBALU 1 the author ran the two together on one
line — a bold 'Zhakwila 1:' followed by plain text — so the block imported as
a paragraph and was the ONE activity of 151 that did not box, printing as
loose body text while its 150 siblings printed in shaded boxes. Promoting it
to a heading lets it box with the rest. (Its trailing full stop, and five more
like it, are dropped by tidyHeadings — which until now never reached a BOX
title, only a plain heading's text; that is fixed in the engine, not here.)
asHead: Zhakwila 1: Kutiyilila kunsañu yakutiya hela yakutaña (mpanji yawankakulula, tuheka, niyishimu) nikwakula malwihu.
_note_numbering: AUTHOR NUMBERING CORRECTED, one sub-topic. The book runs MUTU WANSAÑU WENENI
N.N -> MUTU WANSAÑU WANYANYA N.N.N everywhere, and its topic numbers are a
stable syllabus map (1.4 is CHISELA in every unit that uses it). In CHIBALU 12
the sub-topic under 'MUTU WANSAÑU WENENI 1.4: CHISELA' was typed 'MUTU WANSAÑU
WANYANYA 1.41', a missing dot — the only sub-topic in the book whose number is
not three parts. Set to 1.4.1, the child of the topic directly above it.
Its competence line is numbered 1.3.3.1 and is NOT touched: these are syllabus
strand codes, they legitimately repeat and run out of sequence across the book
(as in the Kiikaonde Grade 1 Teacher's Guide), and nothing in the manuscript
settles which of the two the author meant to change.
_note_spelling: AUTHOR SPELLING CORRECTED. Each of these is a single slip against the author's
own overwhelming usage elsewhere in the same book, counted over the imported
text:
Yilezhi 171 : Yileji 1          — the word that opens most activity steps
atudizi 453 : atidizi 1         — 'learners', the book's commonest noun
toñozhok- stem, 206 times, never with a doubled o : atooñozhoki 1
Ñakwilu 13 : Nakwilu 1          — the n-tilde lost altogether
AUTHOR PUNCTUATION CORRECTED, one section code. The book carries 211 numbered
section codes and 210 of them end '1.3.3.1:'; the competence code in CHIBALU 1's
first sub-topic is the only one typed '1.1.1.1.:', a dot before the colon. It sits
a few pages from its siblings, so the two spellings print in plain sight.
The engine folds the look-alike acute/caron forms (ń, ň) onto the language's
own ñ by itself, but a plain ASCII 'N' cannot be folded automatically — it is
a real letter in Lunda — so that one is corrected here.
'Ñakwilu Yinafuukulewi' (4) is set to 'Ñakwilu Yinafukulewi' (7): the single-u
form is both the author's majority for THIS label and the spelling on his own
returned ZEPH Lunda word form, which is where src/typeset/lexicon/lunda.json
takes 'Ñakwilu Yinafukulewi' from.
NOT corrected, and worth a Lunda speaker's eye: the teaching-aids label is
spelt 'Yikuyuñulu Yinafuukulewi' with a double u in all 70 of its instances,
while the possible-answers label beside it takes the single-u 'Yinafukulewi'.
Both are uniform within their own label, so neither is a slip by the counting
test, but they are the same participle spelt two ways. Left as the author has
it rather than guessed at.
_note_strandcase: AUTHOR CASE CORRECTED, the front-matter strand list. 'Kulumbula mwaya yibalu
ya ntanjikilu' introduces the syllabus strands one by one, and the author typed
its four sub-headings in two different cases — 'Kuhosha nakutiyilila' and
'Kutaña (chakubula kumamatila)' in sentence case, then 'MAZU' and 'KUSONEKA
(CHITUÑI)' in full caps. Four siblings in one list must not print two ways, so
the two caps ones are set to the sentence case the list opens with. The
ALL-CAPS banners inside the body (KUHOSHA NAKUTIYILILA, KUTAÑA, MAZU, KUSONEKA,
KUTAÑA NAKANAÑACHIMA) are a different element in a different place and keep
Each of the two is anchored so it reaches ONLY the front-matter heading:
'KUSONEKA (CHITUÑI' is a prefix no body banner shares (those are a bare
'KUSONEKA'), while a bare 'MAZU' is shared by 16 body banners and, as a prefix,
by all 70 'Mazu Alema' key-word headings — so it matches on the whole text
exactly and takes the first one, which is this front-matter strand.
_note_mazuEdit: The front-matter strand MAZU is singled out with edit + after (main has no recase find/first): the first block containing MAZU after the Kutaña strand heading is that strand, not MAZU ATACHI or a body banner.
_note_references: The reference list prints seven citations, but the author pressed Return after
the URL in four of them, so '(Accessed: 25 January 2026). (For … context)' fell
into a paragraph of its own and those four printed as two blocks while the
other three printed as one. Rejoined so every citation is one paragraph.

_note_images: PRINT RESOLUTION. The cover picture is the only photograph in the book, and the
author placed it twice — once on the front cover and once on the back of the cover
spread. Both placements are the SAME bitmap (word/media/image1.png and image2.png
are byte-identical, one sha256), and both printed at 197 DPI, well under the 300
DPI CLAUDE.md requires at final print size.
Upscaled with Real-ESRGAN (realesrgan-x4plus, -t 128) and resampled back down to
the pixels the target needs, by tools/upscale-images.js:
Only one ESRGAN pass was run. The second entry is the first one’s output copied
across: the inputs are the same bytes, the model and tile size are the same, so the
second pass could only have produced the same file.
Only `src` is set, so nothing moves on the page: the printed size comes from Word’s
own extent, not from the file’s pixel width.
